rationale: Neither candidate hits the ground truth's core ask (a 3-way BNSD/BSND/plain-torch perf comparison), but both independently surface a stronger, related issue: the new shared helper isn't wired into sibling BNSD call sites (qwen3_code_predictor.py, 310P patch), echoing the reviewer's original 'make it a shared util' spirit. X presents this more rigorously (concrete batch/head math, an honest either/or framing of what it implies) and pairs it with sharply verified findings (a demonstrated ndim!=4 failure mode, a precise diagnosis of why the test doesn't cover the batch*heads gate) with concrete suggested fixes/tests. Y covers similar ground but split into more fragmented, noisier findings, includes internally inconsistent claims (its own 'Validated' bullet says code_predictor avoids the constraint at tested concurrency, then the finding claims it's still at risk), and leans on dense evidence-dump prose that's harder to act on directly.
